To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) GraphGen is a novel system that provides in situ querying and analysis of graphs extracted from existing data sources, (2) it provides a unified view of graph data management and graph analytics, and (3) it is the first system to provide in situ graph querying/analytics.
We present the design and implementation of a novel framework, GraphGen, that enables in situ graph querying, analysis, and visualization of relational data.

we present a framework for in situ graph querying/analyzing, called GraphGen that uses a declarative view definition and execution language, and that enables a broad spectrum of users to analyze "hidden graphs" present in their databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of in situ querying and analysis of graphs that are present as a "side-effect" of other data processing tasks.

the following question: How can we provide an in situ, unified, and extensible framework for querying and analyzing graph data in a way that is flexible enough to support a wide range of use cases and that is tightly integrated with existing database systems?
enabling users to query and analyze graphs without having to store them in a graph database, and to do so using a general purpose, reusable, and flexible framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
graph querying and analytics is a rapidly growing field, that has the potential to impact many domains, and that is currently fragmented and lacks a clear unifying theme.
graph querying and analytics is a very exciting and important research topic that will continue to grow and gain prominence, and the work done sofar is just the tip of the iceberg.
graph querying and analytics is finally starting to take root in the data management community, and that GraphGen is a step towards a unifying framework for in situ graph analytics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a framework to enable users to declaratively extract and query large graphs that may be hidden in existing databases (RDBMSs or otherwise) using a subgraph centric, in situ approach.

GraphGen enables in situ graph querying, mining, and analysis over data in existing data sources, and is a unifying abstraction for a wide spectrum of use cases, and a wide range of graph data management systems and approaches.
the graphgen framework is an attempt to provide a unified framework for in situ graph querying, analytics and mining, and graph data virtualization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the graph querying and analytics problem space is much more diverse than is commonly recognized.
the graph data management landscape can benefit from a unifying framework that allows for in situ graph querying/analysis of data stored in heterogeneous data sources.
graph querying and analytics should be treated as a first class data management problem and not just a specialized niche.
